children: The latest win strengthens the company's infrastructure portfolio as first-half order inflows reach Rs 7,589 crore in FY27

Dilip Buildcon has secured a Rs 419.47 crore contract from Gurugram Metro Rail (GMRL) for the construction of a depot-cum-workshop for the Gurugram Metro corridor. The order covers civil, architectural and electrical and mechanical (E&M) works for the elevated metro corridor at Sector 33 in Gurugram, with the project scheduled for completion within 21 months, the company said in an exchange filing.

The contract value includes goods and services tax (GST). Dilip Buildcon said neither its promoters nor promoter group companies have any interest in the awarding entity and clarified that the contract does not fall under related-party transactions. The order adds to the company's infrastructure portfolio as it continues to build its project pipeline.

The latest order win comes days after Dilip Buildcon reported a record order book of Rs 33,081 crore as of September 30, 2026. The figure was 19 per cent higher than Rs 27,691 crore at the end of June and 15 per cent above Rs 28,830 crore recorded at the end of March.

Roads and highways accounted for 15.6 per cent of the total order book, reflecting the company's efforts to diversify beyond its traditional business segment. The order book is approximately 3.6 times the lower end of its FY27 standalone revenue guidance of Rs 9,107 crore, which implies growth of around 30 per cent over the Rs 7,005 crore reported in FY26.

The company secured fresh orders worth Rs 7,321 crore during the September quarter, taking its first-half order inflows to Rs 7,589 crore. This represents around 76 per cent of the lower end of its full-year order inflow target of Rs 10,000 crore, indicating that the company has secured a substantial portion of its targeted order additions in the first half of FY27.

Dilip Buildcon reported a 52.8 per cent year-on-year decline in consolidated net profit to Rs 101 crore in the September quarter, compared with Rs 214 crore in the corresponding period last year. The decline came despite an increase in revenue from operations, which rose 16.8 per cent to Rs 2,250.4 crore from Rs 1,926 crore in the year-ago quarter.

Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) declined 6.8 per cent to Rs 439 crore from Rs 471 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The company's EBITDA margin also contracted to 19.5 per cent in the second quarter of FY27 from 24.5 per cent a year earlier, indicating pressure on operating profitability despite higher revenue.
Shares of Dilip Buildcon closed at Rs 384.30 on the BSE on Thursday, November 19, declining Rs 1.30, or 0.34 per cent.
